projects.title: Example: reviving old tomato seed
projects.question: Can a cheap home treatment bring five-year-old tomato seed back above 80% germination?
projects.summary: Soaking alone did not get there. **Priming** with a salt solution is the strongest lead so far: the priming curve found a clear optimum at 24 h, and the check on a fresh holdout batch is running now. Temperature work is paused on a mixed result.

projects.title: Example: bird feeder placement
projects.question: Do feeder visits drop when the feeder moves two metres away from cover?
projects.summary: Closed. Moving the feeder made no clear difference to visits.

nodes.title: Bring old tomato seed back above 80% germination
nodes.asked: Five-year-old seed of a rare variety sprouts at about 45%. Find a cheap treatment that brings it above 80% without new equipment.

nodes.title: Baseline germination of the old batch (baseline)
nodes.asked: How poor is the old seed, measured the same way every later run will be?
nodes.did: Four **control trays** of 50 seeds each on damp paper at room temperature, counted on day 10.
nodes.found:
Germination rate 44% (40 to 49% across trays). Fresh seed of the same variety: 91%.

| batch | trays | rate |
|---|---|---|
| old | 4 | 44% |
| fresh | 2 | 91% |
nodes.verdict: The old batch sprouts at 44%, so there is real room to recover.
nodes.next: Use these trays as the control in every run.

nodes.title: Just buy new seed
nodes.asked: The cheapest fix is to replace the batch.
nodes.next: Overtaken by the goal itself: the variety is rare, so the point is to recover this batch.

nodes.title: Sample size check (power-check)
nodes.asked: Are four trays per arm enough to see a 15-point gain?
nodes.did: Simulated 10,000 runs with the baseline spread. Registered rule: pass if power is at least 0.8 for a 15-point gain.
nodes.found: Power 0.86 with four trays per arm, 0.97 with eight.
nodes.verdict: Four trays per arm are enough.

nodes.title: Compare two potting mixes instead of paper
nodes.asked: Paper is not how the seed is grown in practice. A potting mix might change the picture.
nodes.next: Two more trays per arm and three extra weeks. No new equipment.

nodes.title: Soaking treatments
nodes.asked: Does water uptake before sowing help old seed?
nodes.verdict: Closed after two runs: soaking helps a little, never enough.

nodes.title: Water soak for 12 h (soak-12)
nodes.asked: Does a plain water soak raise the germination rate?
nodes.did: Seeds soaked 12 h in tap water at 20 C, then sown as in the baseline. Registered rule: pass if the rate beats the control tray by at least 10 points.
nodes.verdict: Soaking helps, but not enough to reach 80%.

nodes.title: Water soak for 24 h (soak-24)
nodes.asked: Does a longer soak help more?
nodes.did: Same as soak-12, with 24 h in water.
nodes.found: Rate 47%. Several seeds showed mould by day 6.
nodes.verdict: A longer soak does not help: mould cancels the gain.

nodes.title: Hydrogen peroxide rinse against mould
nodes.asked: A dilute rinse might stop the mould seen in soak-24.
nodes.next: The mould only appeared past 12 h, and the 12 h soak already works without it.

nodes.title: Compost tea soak
nodes.asked: Microbes in compost tea are said to help old seed.
nodes.next: Overtaken by seed priming, which tests the same idea with a controlled solution.

nodes.title: Temperature
nodes.asked: Is room temperature holding the old seed back?
nodes.verdict: Paused on a mixed result and a lost run.

nodes.title: Heat mat at 26 C (heatmat-26)
nodes.asked: Does warmth raise the rate, or only the speed?
nodes.did: Trays on a heat mat set to 26 C, otherwise as the baseline. Two outcomes registered: speed (days to half the final count) and final rate.
nodes.found:
- Speed: **passed**, 4.1 days against 6.3 for control
- Final rate: **failed**, 49% against 44% (the rule needed 54%)
nodes.verdict: Seeds sprout faster, but not more of them.

nodes.title: Day and night temperature cycle
nodes.asked: A 26/18 C day and night cycle is closer to spring outdoors.
nodes.next: Needs a timer plug (about 15 euro) and three weeks.

nodes.title: Thermostat controller for the heat mat
nodes.asked: The mat drifted between 24 and 29 C. A controller would remove that noise.
nodes.next: About 25 euro. Only worth it if temperature work resumes.

nodes.title: Cold stratification for two weeks (strat-2w)
nodes.asked: Some seeds need a cold period first. Does tomato seed?
nodes.did: Planned 14 days at 4 C in a fridge, then sown as the baseline.
nodes.found: Stopped on day 5: the fridge failed and the trays warmed to 18 C.
nodes.verdict: No result: the run was lost.
nodes.next: Repeat only with a reliable fridge.

nodes.title: Seed priming
nodes.asked: Controlled partial hydration (priming) is used commercially on old seed. Can a home version work?

nodes.title: Priming curve with salt solution (prime-curve)
nodes.asked: How long should the seed be primed?
nodes.did: Five priming times (6, 12, 24, 36, 48 h) in a salt solution, dried, then sown as the baseline. No pass rule: this maps the curve.
nodes.found:
Peak at **24 h**: 76%. At 6 h: 52%. At 48 h: 61%.

1. The curve rises steeply to 24 h.
2. It falls slowly after that.
nodes.verdict: Priming for 24 h is the best setting found so far.
nodes.next: Check 24 h on seed it was not tuned on.

nodes.title: Tetrazolium viability test
nodes.asked: Stain seeds to tell dead seed from dormant seed.
nodes.next: Needs a lab chemical and a microscope.

nodes.title: Priming at 24 h on a holdout batch (prime-holdout)
nodes.asked: Does the 24 h setting hold on seed it was not tuned on?
nodes.did: A second old batch, kept aside since March as the holdout batch. Eight trays per arm. Registered rule: pass if primed seed beats control by at least 20 points.
nodes.user_note: Check tray 7: the lid was loose on day 2.

nodes.title: Red light during germination
nodes.asked: Red light speeds up germination in some species.
nodes.next: Needs an LED strip (about 20 euro). Run after prime-holdout.

nodes.title: Clay seed coating after priming
nodes.asked: Coating primed seed could keep it viable longer in storage.
nodes.next: Needs bentonite clay and one month of storage before the test.

nodes.title: Priming plus heat mat (prime-heat)
nodes.asked: Priming raises the rate and the mat raises the speed. Do they add up?
nodes.did: Registered, not run: four trays per arm, a 2 by 2 design.

nodes.title: Write-up
nodes.asked: A short methods note other seed savers can follow.

nodes.title: First draft of the methods note (draft-1)
nodes.asked: Write down the method while it is fresh.
nodes.did: Six pages: methods and the priming curve.
nodes.found: The results section waits for prime-holdout.
nodes.verdict: Draft ready; results wait for the holdout run.

nodes.title: Submit to a seed savers newsletter
nodes.asked: A short note could reach other seed savers.

nodes.title: Record a video of the method
nodes.asked: Video is easier to follow than text.
nodes.next: Too much time for little gain.

nodes.title: Do feeder visits drop away from cover?
nodes.asked: Small birds may avoid a feeder far from the hedge.

nodes.title: Move the feeder 2 m from the hedge (move-2m)
nodes.asked: Do visits per hour fall after the move?
nodes.did: Counted visits for 30 minutes each morning, one week before and one week after.

nodes.title: Use a trail camera instead of counting by eye
nodes.asked: Counting by eye misses quick visits.

terms.short: Share of sown seeds that sprout by day 10.
terms.definition: The number of seeds with a visible root by day 10, divided by the number sown. Every run in this project counts on the same day, so rates can be compared across runs.

terms.short: Untreated old seed sown alongside every run.
terms.definition: A tray of the same old batch with no treatment, sown on the same day and in the same place as the treated trays. A gain only counts against the control from the same run.

terms.short: Seeds left in plain water before sowing.
terms.definition: Seeds sit in tap water for a set time and are sown wet. Unlike **priming**, they are not dried again.

terms.short: Partial hydration, then drying, before sowing.
terms.definition: Seeds take up water in a salt solution that stops them from sprouting, then are dried and stored. When sown, they start faster and more evenly.

terms.short: A cold, damp period that breaks dormancy in some seeds.
terms.definition: Seeds are kept damp at 2 to 5 C for weeks before sowing. Many wild plants need it; garden tomatoes usually do not.

terms.short: Seed kept aside and never used to choose a setting.
terms.definition: A second old batch stored since March and not used in any tuning run. A setting chosen on the first batch is only trusted if it also works here.

terms.short: Whether a seed is alive and able to sprout.
terms.definition: A seed can be alive but dormant, or dead. Germination counts cannot tell the two apart; a stain test can.

terms.short: The pass condition written down before a run.
terms.definition: Before each run, the pass condition is written in the run sheet with its threshold. The verdict follows the rule, even when the result looks close.

terms.short: A bird landing on the feeder and taking food.
terms.definition: One landing counts as one visit, however long the bird stays.
